patrick-john.s: Patrick John was a Dominican trade unionist and politician of the Dominica Labour Party who became the island's first prime minister on independence in 1978. His government faced strikes and mass protests, and he was forced from office in 1979.

patrick-tonyn.s: Patrick Tonyn was a British army officer who was governor of the Province of East Florida from 1774 to 1785. During the American Revolutionary War he made the colony a refuge for loyalists and a base for raids into Georgia.

pau-claris.s: Pau Claris was a Catalan cleric, canon of La Seu d'Urgell, who was president of the Generalitat of Catalonia during the Reapers' War. As a royal army advanced on Barcelona, he proclaimed a Catalan Republic under French protection in January 1641, and days later placed…

paul-kagame.s: Paul Kagame is a Rwandan soldier and politician who commanded the Rwandan Patriotic Front forces that ended the genocide against the Tutsi in 1994. He was vice-president and defence minister before becoming president in 2000.

paul-the-deacon.s: Paul the Deacon was a Benedictine monk and historian from a noble Lombard family of Friuli, educated at the royal court of Pavia. After the Frankish conquest he spent some years at Charlemagne's court before returning to Monte Cassino.

pavel-tsitsianov.s: Pavel Tsitsianov was a Russian general of Georgian descent who commanded Russian forces in the Caucasus from 1802. He stormed Ganja in January 1804, killing Javad Khan, and forced several khanates to accept Russian protection.

payen-the-butler.s: Payen the Butler was a Crusader noble, butler of the kings of Jerusalem, who became lord of Oultrejordain, the lands east of the Jordan. In 1142 he built the great castle of Kerak on a ridge east of the Dead Sea, which became the centre of the lordship and controlled the…

paynda-khan-tanoli.s: Paynda Khan Tanoli was chief of the Tanoli tribe and ruler of Amb, in the Hazara region of today's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, in the early 19th century. He resisted the expanding Sikh Empire, fighting its governors of Hazara, and lost part of his lands to them.

peace-of-pressburg-1805.s: The Peace of Pressburg was signed on 26 December 1805 at Pressburg (Bratislava) between France and Austria after Napoleon's victory at Austerlitz. Austria ceded Venetia to Napoleon's Kingdom of Italy and Tyrol, Burgau and other lands to Bavaria and Württemberg, which became…

pearl-river.s: The Pearl River is the great river system of southern China, formed by the West, North and East rivers, which meet in a broad delta at Guangzhou before reaching the South China Sea. In ancient times its western branches linked the highlands of Guizhou with the lowlands of Nanyue.

pearl-river-mississippi-louisiana.s: The Pearl River flows about 790 kilometres through Mississippi and along the Louisiana border into Lake Borgne and the Gulf of Mexico. Its lower course separated the Florida Parishes, part of the short-lived Republic of West Florida in 1810, from the lands to the east that…

pedakomati-vema-reddi.s: Pedakomati Vema Reddi was a king of the Reddi dynasty of coastal Andhra, ruling from Kondavidu from about 1403 to 1420. A patron of letters and himself an author in Sanskrit, he kept the great Telugu poet Srinatha at his court.

pedda-soma-bhupal.s: Pedda Soma Bhupal was a local chief who founded the Gadwal samasthan around 1663 in the land between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, in today's Telangana. He built the fort at Gadwal, which became the seat of a family that ruled as tributaries of the Nizams of Hyderabad…

pedrarias-davila.s: Pedrarias Dávila was a Spanish soldier and colonial governor who arrived in 1514 as governor of Castilla de Oro, on the Isthmus of Panama. His rule was marked by violent raids on Indigenous peoples and by rivalry with Vasco Núñez de Balboa, whom he had executed in 1519.

pedro-caetano-pereira.s: Pedro Caetano Pereira was a ruler of Makanga, an Afro-Portuguese warlord state north of the Zambezi near Tete in Mozambique. With his father Gonçalo Caetano Pereira he built the state in the mid-19th century as the Portuguese prazo system broke down, ruling from fortified…

pedro-de-mendoza.s: Pedro de Mendoza was a Spanish nobleman and conquistador to whom Charles V granted the Río de la Plata governorate in 1534. He led a large expedition that founded the first settlement of Buenos Aires in 1536, but hunger and attacks by local peoples forced most settlers away.

pedro-de-valdivia.s: Pedro de Valdivia was a Spanish conquistador who served under Francisco Pizarro in Peru and then led an expedition south, founding Santiago in February 1541. As the first royal governor of Chile he founded Concepción, Valdivia and other towns and pushed into Mapuche lands.

pelopidas.s: Pelopidas was a Theban general and statesman who led the exiles who freed Thebes from its Spartan garrison in 379 BCE. With Epaminondas he revived the Boeotian League, commanded the Sacred Band at Leuctra in 371 BCE and helped make Thebes the leading power in Greece.

peoples-national-movement.s: The People's National Movement is a political party of Trinidad and Tobago founded by the historian Eric Williams in 1956. It won the elections that year, led the colony to independence in 1962 and governed without a break until 1986.

peoples-revolutionary-government-grenada.s: The People's Revolutionary Government was the socialist government of Grenada formed after the New Jewel Movement under Maurice Bishop overthrew Eric Gairy on 13 March 1979. It built close ties with Cuba and began an international airport at Point Salines.

pepin-ii-of-aquitaine.s: Pepin II of Aquitaine was the son of Pepin I, king of Aquitaine, and a grandson of Louis the Pious. Passed over when his father died in 838, he fought a long war against his uncle Charles the Bald for Aquitaine and held much of it in the 840s.

pepin-of-italy.s: Pepin of Italy was a son of Charlemagne, born Carloman, who was crowned king of Italy in 781 to rule the conquered Lombard kingdom. He campaigned against the Avars and the Duchy of Benevento.

perdiccas-ii-of-macedon.s: Perdiccas II was king of Macedon from about 448 to about 413 BCE, who repeatedly changed sides between Athens and Sparta in the Peloponnesian War. In 432 BCE he persuaded the Chalcidian towns to revolt from the Delian League and to concentrate their people at Olynthus,…

pericles.s: Pericles was an Athenian statesman and general who dominated the democracy from the 450s until his death in 429 BCE. He used the tribute of the Delian League, whose treasury had been moved to Athens, to fund the building programme of the Acropolis, including the Parthenon.

perth-amboy.s: Perth Amboy is a port city in New Jersey at the mouth of the Raritan River on Raritan Bay. Scottish proprietors founded it in the 1680s as the capital of East Jersey, naming it after the Earl of Perth.

petar-dobrovic.s: Petar Dobrović was a Serbian painter from Pécs and one of the leading modernist painters of Yugoslavia. When the Treaty of Trianon returned the Baranya region to Hungary, he was proclaimed president of the short-lived Serbian-Hungarian Baranya-Baja Republic in August 1921.

petar-kresimir-iv.s: Petar Krešimir IV was king of Croatia from 1058 to 1074, of the Trpimirović dynasty. He brought the Byzantine towns and islands of Dalmatia under his rule and styled himself king of Croatia and Dalmatia.

peter-chester.s: Peter Chester was a British army officer who served as governor of the Province of West Florida from 1770 until its capture by Spanish forces in 1781. He governed from Pensacola alongside an elected assembly, with which he often quarrelled.

peter-fraser.s: Peter Fraser was a Scottish-born New Zealand Labour politician who was prime minister of New Zealand from 1940 to 1949. He led the country through the Second World War, built on the welfare state founded under Michael Joseph Savage, and helped draft the United Nations Charter…

peter-iii-of-russia.s: Peter III was emperor of Russia for six months in 1762, a grandson of Peter the Great raised in Holstein. In 1745 he married Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst, who took the name Catherine.

peter-kenilorea.s: Sir Peter Kenilorea was a Solomon Islands teacher and politician who became chief minister in 1976 and the first prime minister when the islands became independent from Britain on 7 July 1978. He served as prime minister again in the mid-1980s and later as speaker of the…

peter-tali-coleman.s: Peter Tali Coleman was an American Samoan politician who became the first person of Samoan descent to be appointed governor, in 1956, and the territory's first elected governor in 1977. He served further elected terms until 1993 and also held senior posts in the Trust…

peteris-stucka.s: Pēteris Stučka was a Latvian Bolshevik lawyer and writer who led the Soviet government of Latvia proclaimed in December 1918. His regime took Riga in January 1919 and ruled much of the country with harsh revolutionary measures, but it was driven out by Latvian, Baltic German…

petro-kalnyshevsky.s: Petro Kalnyshevsky was the last otaman of the Zaporozhian Sich, holding the office for most years from 1762 to 1775. When Catherine II's army destroyed the Sich in 1775 he was arrested and exiled to the Solovetsky Monastery in the White Sea, where he was held for decades and…

petro-shelest.s: Petro Shelest was first secretary of the Communist Party of Ukraine from 1963 to 1972. While loyal to Moscow, he defended Ukrainian economic interests and tolerated some promotion of Ukrainian language and culture.

phanariotes.s: The Phanariotes were members of wealthy Greek families of the Phanar, the Greek quarter of Constantinople around the Ecumenical Patriarchate. From the late 17th century they served the Ottoman state as dragomans, and from the 1710s the sultans appointed them princes of…

phaya-choeng.s: Phaya Choeng is the founder of the Tai Lue kingdom of Sipsong Panna in the upper Mekong valley of southern Yunnan. According to Tai Lue chronicles, he united the Tai principalities of the region in 1180 and founded his capital at Chiang Hung, modern Jinghong.

philaretos-brachamios.s: Philaretos Brachamios was an Armenian general in Byzantine service who, after the defeat at Manzikert in 1071, built an independent principality in Cilicia and northern Syria. At its height it included Antioch, Edessa, Melitene and Marash.

philip-francis-little.s: Philip Francis Little was a lawyer from Prince Edward Island who became the first premier of the Colony of Newfoundland when responsible government was introduced in 1855. Leader of the Liberal Party, which drew strong support from Irish Catholics, he served until 1858 and…

philip-i-of-taranto.s: Philip I of Taranto was an Angevin prince, son of Charles II of Naples, who received the Principality of Taranto in 1294. He also held the Angevin claims to the Kingdom of Albania and the Principality of Achaea and, through his marriage to Catherine of Valois, the title of…

philip-iii-of-france.s: Philip III, called the Bold, was king of France from 1270 to 1285, the son of Louis IX. He inherited the lands of the counts of Toulouse, and in 1274 he handed the Comtat Venaissin, which had passed to the French crown after the Albigensian Crusade, to Pope Gregory X.

philip-iii-of-spain.s: Philip III was king of Spain and, as Philip II, king of Portugal from 1598 to 1621, during the Iberian Union. He left government largely to his favourite, the Duke of Lerma, made peace with England in 1604 and agreed the Twelve Years' Truce with the Dutch in 1609.

philip-duke-of-parma.s: Philip, Duke of Parma, was a son of Philip V of Spain and Elisabeth Farnese who founded the Bourbon-Parma line. Under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle of 1748 he received the duchies of Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla.

philip-of-hachberg-sausenberg.s: Philip of Hachberg-Sausenberg was margrave of Hachberg-Sausenberg in the Breisgau and count of Neuchâtel in the late 15th century. He served the dukes of Burgundy and then the French crown as a soldier and diplomat, holding high offices.

philip-of-milly.s: Philip of Milly was a Crusader noble of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, lord of Nablus, who exchanged it in 1161 for the lordship of Oultrejordain with its castles of Kerak and Montréal. He became Grand Master of the Knights Templar in 1169 and died in 1171.

philip-otto-of-salm.s: Philip Otto of Salm was a count of the Rhinegrave branch of the house of Salm in the Vosges, raised to the rank of prince of the Holy Roman Empire in 1623. The elevation turned his lands, centred on Badonviller and Senones, into the Principality of Salm.

philip-sigismund-of-brunswick-wolfenbutt.s: Philip Sigismund of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel was a Lutheran prince of the House of Welf who administered the prince-bishoprics of Verden from 1586 and Osnabrück from 1591 until his death in 1623. As administrator he consolidated the Reformation in Verden, where Lutheran rulers…

philip-the-handsome.s: Philip the Handsome was the son of Emperor Maximilian I and Mary of Burgundy and inherited the Burgundian Netherlands as a child in 1482, with his father as regent. His marriage to Joanna of Castile made him king of Castile in 1506, but he died that year.

philip-v-of-spain.s: Philip V was king of Spain from 1700 to 1746, the first of the Bourbon dynasty. A grandson of Louis XIV, he inherited the throne as Philip of Anjou under the will of Charles II, which caused the War of the Spanish Succession.

philip-vi-of-france.s: Philip VI was king of France from 1328 to 1350, the first of the House of Valois. His accession over the claim of Edward III of England led to the Hundred Years' War, in which he was defeated at Crécy in 1346.

philip-william-elector-palatine.s: Philip William was duke of Palatinate-Neuburg and of Jülich and Berg from 1653, and Elector Palatine from 1685 to 1690. When the Simmern line of the Palatinate died out in 1685 he inherited the electorate, bringing a Catholic dynasty to the Palatinate.

philippe-leclerc-de-hauteclocque.s: Philippe Leclerc de Hauteclocque was a French general who joined the Free French in 1940. From Chad he led raids into Italian Libya, taking Kufra in 1941 and the Fezzan in 1942–1943, then commanded the 2nd Armoured Division, which liberated Paris in August 1944 and Strasbourg…

philippe-pastour-de-costebelle.s: Philippe Pastour de Costebelle was a French officer and the last governor of Plaisance, the French colony on Newfoundland, from 1706. After the Treaty of Utrecht of 1713 handed Newfoundland to Britain, he moved the settlers to Île Royale (Cape Breton Island) and became its…

philippine-revolution.s: The Philippine Revolution was the armed struggle against Spanish rule launched by the Katipunan secret society in August 1896. After a truce in 1897 it revived in 1898 under Emilio Aguinaldo during the Spanish–American War, leading to the declaration of independence on 12 June…

philippine-american-war.s: The Philippine–American War was fought between the United States and the First Philippine Republic after Spain ceded the islands to the United States in 1898. Fighting broke out in February 1899, and Filipino forces turned to guerrilla warfare.

phocaeans.s: The Phocaeans were the Ionian Greeks of Phocaea on the Aegean coast of Anatolia, famed seafarers who explored the western Mediterranean. They founded Massalia (Marseille) around 600 BCE and Alalia on Corsica, and traded with Tartessos in southern Iberia.

phra-bang.s: The Phra Bang is a gilded standing Buddha image, the palladium of the Lao monarchy, after which the city of Luang Prabang is named. Tradition holds that Fa Ngum brought it from Cambodia in the 14th century together with Theravada Buddhism.

phuntsog-namgyal.s: Phuntsog Namgyal was the first Chogyal, or king, of Sikkim, consecrated at Yuksom in 1642 by three Tibetan Buddhist lamas. Founder of the Namgyal dynasty, he organised a Buddhist monarchy over the Bhutia and Lepcha peoples and set up the administration of the kingdom.

piero-soderini.s: Piero Soderini was a Florentine statesman elected gonfaloniere of justice for life in 1502, leading the republic restored after the expulsion of the Medici in 1494. With Niccolò Machiavelli as his secretary he created a citizen militia.

pierre-belain-desnambuc.s: Pierre Belain d'Esnambuc was a Norman sea captain who founded the first permanent French colony in the Caribbean. He landed on Saint Christopher in 1625 and, backed by Cardinal Richelieu's Compagnie de Saint-Christophe, shared the island with the English.

pierre-buyoya.s: Pierre Buyoya was a Tutsi army officer who twice seized power in Burundi, ruling from 1987 to 1993 and again from 1996 to 2003. In his first term he opened the way to multiparty elections, which he lost to Melchior Ndadaye in 1993.

pierre-dugua-de-mons.s: Pierre Dugua de Mons was a Huguenot merchant and nobleman from Saintonge who held the French royal monopoly of the fur trade in North America. In 1604 he led the expedition, with Samuel de Champlain, that wintered on Saint Croix Island, and in 1605 he founded Port-Royal, the…

pierre-laval.s: Pierre Laval was a French politician who served as prime minister in the 1930s and became the leading figure of collaboration in Vichy France. As head of government from 1942 to 1944 he worked closely with Nazi Germany, sending French workers to the Reich and assisting the…

pierre-mendes-france.s: Pierre Mendès France was a French Radical politician and prime minister from June 1954 to February 1955. After the defeat at Dien Bien Phu he negotiated the Geneva Accords that ended the First Indochina War, and he opened the path to Tunisian autonomy.

pierre-nkurunziza.s: Pierre Nkurunziza was a Hutu former rebel commander of the CNDD-FDD who became president of Burundi in 2005, after the civil war. His decision to seek a disputed third term in 2015 led to protests, a failed coup attempt and a wave of repression and emigration.

pierre-poivre.s: Pierre Poivre was a French horticulturist and administrator who served as intendant of the Isle de France (Mauritius) and Bourbon from 1767 to 1772. He smuggled clove and nutmeg plants out of the Dutch-controlled Moluccas to break the Dutch spice monopoly, and developed the…

pilaji-rao-gaekwad.s: Pilaji Rao Gaekwad was a Maratha commander who founded the power of the Gaekwad family in Gujarat. Serving under the Dabhade senapatis, he seized Songadh in 1721 and raided Mughal Gujarat from there until he was assassinated in 1732.

pillar-of-eliseg.s: The Pillar of Eliseg is a stone cross shaft near Llangollen in north-east Wales, raised in the 9th century by Cyngen ap Cadell, king of Powys, in honour of his great-grandfather Eliseg. Its now largely illegible Latin inscription traced the royal line of Powys back to…

pinnata-castra.s: Pinnata Castra, 'the winged camp', is a place in north-east Scotland listed in Ptolemy's Geography of about 150 CE among the towns of the Vacomagi. Its location is uncertain: it has been identified with the promontory fort at Burghead on the Moray coast and with the Roman…

pino-iii-ordelaffi.s: Pino III Ordelaffi was lord of Forlì in Romagna from 1466 until his death in 1480, one of the last rulers of the Ordelaffi family that had governed the city since the 13th century. He strengthened the fortress of Ravaldino.

pippin-of-herstal.s: Pippin of Herstal was mayor of the palace of Austrasia and, after his victory over Neustria at Tertry in 687, the real ruler of the whole Frankish kingdom under figurehead Merovingian kings. He fought the Frisians under Redbad and took Dorestad and Utrecht around 690.

pir-panjal-range.s: The Pir Panjal Range is a chain of the Lesser Himalaya that separates the Kashmir valley from the hills of Jammu and the Punjab plains. Its passes, above all the Pir Panjal Pass on the Mughal road, carried traffic into Kashmir for centuries, and small hill states such as…

piri-mehmed-pasha-ramadanid.s: Piri Mehmed Pasha was a 16th-century ruler of the Ramadanid family, the Turkmen dynasty that governed Adana in Cilicia as hereditary Ottoman governors after 1517. He is remembered chiefly as a builder: he completed the Great Mosque complex of Adana begun by his predecessor,…

pirmin.s: Saint Pirmin was a wandering bishop and monastic founder in the Frankish realm. In 724, with the support of Charles Martel, he founded the Benedictine abbey of Reichenau on Lake Constance, and in 727 Murbach in the Vosges, before founding Hornbach, where he died.

pithana.s: Pithana was a king of Kussara in central Anatolia in the 18th century BCE. According to the inscription of his son Anitta, he captured the trading city of Nesa (Kanesh) by night and treated its people well.

pitu-guli.s: Pitu Guli was an Aromanian revolutionary of the Internal Macedonian-Adrianople Revolutionary Organisation from Kruševo. In the Ilinden Uprising of August 1903 he led rebel bands that took the town and helped proclaim the Kruševo Republic.

pope-pius-ix.s: Pope Pius IX reigned from 1846 to 1878, the longest pontificate in history. Driven briefly from Rome by the revolution of 1848, he lost most of the Papal States to the Kingdom of Italy in 1860 and Rome itself in 1870, after which he called himself a prisoner in the Vatican.

placido-de-castro.s: Plácido de Castro was a Brazilian soldier and surveyor who led the rubber tappers of Acre in the Acrean Revolution against Bolivia in 1902–1903. His capture of Puerto Alonso prepared the Treaty of Petrópolis of 1903, by which Brazil acquired Acre.

plaek-phibunsongkhram.s: Plaek Phibunsongkhram was a Thai army officer, one of the leaders of the 1932 revolution that ended absolute monarchy, and prime minister from 1938 to 1944 and 1948 to 1957. He promoted a nationalist programme, renamed Siam as Thailand in 1939 and allied the country with Japan…

platt-amendment.s: The Platt Amendment was a 1901 rider to a United States army appropriations act that set the conditions for ending the American occupation of Cuba. Written into the Cuban constitution, it gave the United States the right to intervene in Cuba and to lease naval stations,…

pol-pot.s: Pol Pot was the leader of the Khmer Rouge and of Democratic Kampuchea from 1975 to 1979. His regime emptied the cities, abolished money and religion, and forced the population into rural labour camps, causing the deaths of some 1.5 to 2 million Cambodians by execution,…

polemon-ii-of-pontus.s: Polemon II was the last client king of Pontus, a grandson of Queen Pythodorida. The emperor Caligula gave him the kingdom in 38 CE, and Claudius added part of Cilicia.

polish-ukrainian-war.s: The Polish–Ukrainian War was fought from November 1918 to July 1919 over Eastern Galicia, after the collapse of Austria-Hungary. It began with fighting in Lviv between Polish residents and the forces of the West Ukrainian People's Republic.

pomare-iv.s: Pōmare IV was queen of Tahiti for fifty years, from 1827 to 1877. Her reign was dominated by rivalry between British Protestant missionaries and French Catholic priests, which led France to impose a protectorate in 1842 and to fight the Franco-Tahitian War of 1844–1847.

pomponius-mela.s: Pomponius Mela was a Roman geographer from southern Hispania, the earliest Latin author of a surviving geographical work. His De Chorographia, written around 43 CE, describes the coasts of the known world, with notes on peoples and places.

ponhea-yat.s: Ponhea Yat was a Khmer king traditionally regarded as the last ruler of Angkor. After the Siamese of Ayutthaya sacked Angkor around 1431, he moved the royal court south and settled it at Phnom Penh, at the confluence of the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers.

pope-alexander-iii.s: Pope Alexander III reigned from 1159 to 1181. For nearly twenty years he resisted Emperor Frederick Barbarossa and a series of imperial antipopes, supporting the Lombard League, whose new city of Alessandria was named after him.

pope-clement-viii.s: Pope Clement VIII reigned from 1592 to 1605. He absolved Henry IV of France in 1595 and brought the Duchy of Ferrara under direct papal rule in 1598, refusing to recognise Cesare d'Este as heir.

pope-gregory-vii.s: Pope Gregory VII, born Hildebrand, reigned from 1073 to 1085 and gave his name to the Gregorian reform. His struggle with Emperor Henry IV over the investiture of bishops led to Henry's penance at Canossa in 1077.

pope-honorius-iii.s: Pope Honorius III reigned from 1216 to 1227. He confirmed the Dominican order in 1216 and the Franciscan rule in 1223, and promoted the Fifth Crusade.

pope-innocent-iv.s: Pope Innocent IV reigned from 1243 to 1254. At the First Council of Lyon in 1245 he declared Emperor Frederick II deposed, and he sent envoys to the Mongols.

pope-leo-ix.s: Pope Leo IX, born Bruno of Egisheim-Dagsburg, was bishop of Toul before reigning as pope from 1049 to 1054. He travelled widely to enforce church reform against simony and clerical marriage.

pope-pius-v.s: Pope Pius V, a Dominican and former inquisitor, reigned from 1566 to 1572 and enforced the decrees of the Council of Trent. In 1569 he raised Cosimo I de' Medici to Grand Duke of Tuscany, in 1570 he excommunicated Elizabeth I of England, and he organised the Holy League whose…

pope-sixtus-iv.s: Pope Sixtus IV reigned from 1471 to 1484. He built the Sistine Chapel and refounded the Vatican Library, but was notorious for advancing his nephews, among them Girolamo Riario, for whom he acquired Imola and Forlì.

pope-stephen-ii.s: Pope Stephen II reigned from 752 to 757. When the Lombards took Ravenna and threatened Rome, he crossed the Alps in 753–754, the first pope to do so, and anointed the Frankish king Pepin the Short.

porfirio-diaz.s: Porfirio Díaz was a Mexican general, hero of the war against the French intervention, who seized power in 1876 and ruled almost continuously until 1911. The period, called the Porfiriato, brought railways, mines and foreign investment but also great concentration of land and…

port-vila.s: Port Vila is a port town on the island of Efate and the capital of Vanuatu. In 1889 French and other settlers there declared the short-lived commune of Franceville, independent of both Britain and France.

porto-longone.s: Porto Longone, today Porto Azzurro, is a harbour town on the east coast of Elba. Spain built a large star-shaped fortress there in 1603 and added it to the State of the Presidi, its chain of coastal garrisons in Tuscany, giving the Spanish crown a base beside the Principality…

porto-torres.s: Porto Torres is a port town in north-western Sardinia, the Roman colony of Turris Libisonis. In the Middle Ages it gave its name to the Judicate of Torres (Logudoro), and its Romanesque basilica of San Gavino is the largest in Sardinia.

potatau-te-wherowhero.s: Pōtatau Te Wherowhero was a leading chief of the Waikato tribes and a noted warrior of the Musket Wars. In 1858 he was crowned at Ngāruawāhia as the first Māori King, chosen by the Kīngitanga movement to unite tribes and protect Māori land against sales to settlers.

prague-castle.s: Prague Castle is a vast castle complex above the Vltava in Prague, founded in the late 9th century by the Přemyslid duke Bořivoj. It has been the seat of Bohemian dukes and kings, of Holy Roman emperors, and of Czechoslovak and Czech presidents, and contains St Vitus Cathedral.

pratap-malla.s: Pratap Malla was king of Kantipur (Kathmandu) from 1641 to 1674, the most celebrated ruler of the Malla kingdoms of the Kathmandu valley. A poet who wrote in several languages, he enlarged the Hanuman Dhoka palace, built the Rani Pokhari pond and set up a famous inscription in…

pravahana-jaivali.s: Pravahana Jaivali was a king of Panchala who appears in the Chandogya and Brihadaranyaka Upanishads. In these texts he instructs the Brahmin Uddalaka Aruni and his son Shvetaketu in the doctrine of the five fires and the paths of the dead, one of the earliest statements of the…

pravarasena-ii.s: Pravarasena II was a 5th-century king of the main branch of the Vakataka dynasty in the Deccan, son of Rudrasena II and the Gupta princess Prabhavatigupta. He is credited with the Prakrit poem Setubandha, on Rama's bridge to Lanka, and founded a new capital at Pravarapura.

pravir-chandra-bhanj-deo.s: Pravir Chandra Bhanj Deo was the last ruling Maharaja of Bastar, installed as a child in 1936. After the state merged into India in 1948 he became a champion of the Adivasi peoples of Bastar in disputes over land and forests with the government.

prempeh-ii.s: Prempeh II was Asantehene from 1931 to 1970, succeeding his uncle Prempeh I. In 1935 the British restored the Asante Confederacy and recognised him as its head.

prince-frederick-of-noer.s: Prince Frederick of Noer, of the Augustenburg branch of the Danish royal house, was a leader of the German movement in Schleswig-Holstein. In March 1848 he joined the provisional government at Kiel and took command of its army, seizing the fortress of Rendsburg at the start of…

prince-george-of-greece-and-denmark.n: Prince George of Greece and Denmark
prince-george-of-greece-and-denmark.s: Prince George of Greece and Denmark was the second son of King George I of Greece. In December 1898 the great powers appointed him High Commissioner of the autonomous Cretan State, which he governed from Chania until 1906.

prince-of-transylvania.s: Prince of Transylvania was the title of the rulers of the Principality of Transylvania, first taken by John Sigismund Zápolya when he gave up the Hungarian royal title at the Treaty of Speyer in 1570. The princes were elected by the Transylvanian diet and ruled under Ottoman…

prince-rupert-of-the-rhine.s: Prince Rupert of the Rhine was a nephew of Charles I of England, a Royalist cavalry commander in the English Civil War and later an admiral. A leading backer of the fur-trading voyages to Hudson Bay, he became the first governor of the Hudson's Bay Company when it was…

princes-stone.s: The Prince's Stone is the base of an ancient Roman column that stood at Karnburg in Carinthia, where the princes of Carantania and later the dukes of Carinthia were installed. In the ceremony a free peasant seated on the stone questioned the new ruler in Slovene before handing…

princes-town-ghana.s: Princes Town, known locally as Pokesu, is a coastal village near Cape Three Points in western Ghana. In 1683 the Brandenburg African Company built the fort of Gross Friedrichsburg there, the headquarters of the Brandenburger Gold Coast, which traded in gold and enslaved people…

principality-of-lucca-and-piombino.s: The Principality of Lucca and Piombino was a Napoleonic state in Tuscany created in 1805 for Napoleon's sister Elisa Bonaparte and her husband Felice Baciocchi. It replaced the old Republic of Lucca and absorbed the Principality of Piombino.

prithvideva-ii.s: Prithvideva II was a king of the Kalachuri dynasty of Ratanpur in Chhattisgarh in the 12th century. He extended the kingdom and fought the Eastern Gangas of Kalinga, and numerous inscriptions and coins survive from his reign.

prithvipal-sen.s: Prithvipal Sen was the last king of Palpa, a hill kingdom in western Nepal ruled by the Sen dynasty. Palpa had stayed independent of Gorkha through marriage alliances, but in 1806 Prithvipal Sen was lured to Kathmandu and killed in the massacre that followed the murder of Rana…

privilegium-minus.s: The Privilegium Minus was a charter issued by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa in 1156 that raised the Margraviate of Austria to a duchy. It compensated Henry II Jasomirgott of the Babenberg family for giving up Bavaria, and granted the new duchy unusual rights, including…

prolaya-vema-reddi.s: Prolaya Vema Reddi was the founder of the Reddi kingdom in coastal Andhra. A former follower of the Kakatiyas, he joined the Musunuri Nayaks in the revolt against the Delhi Sultanate and around 1325 established his own rule, with his capital at Addanki.

provenzan-salvani.s: Provenzan Salvani was the leader of the Ghibelline government of Siena in the mid-13th century. He was among the commanders when Siena crushed Florence at the Battle of Montaperti in 1260, and he dominated the city afterwards.

przemko-of-scinawa.s: Przemko of Ścinawa was a Silesian Piast duke, a son of Henry III of Głogów, who received Ścinawa on the Oder as his share of his father's lands. He was one of the first rulers of the small Duchy of Ścinawa and was killed in 1289 at the Battle of Siewierz, fighting in the…

przemysl-ii.s: Przemysł II was duke of Greater Poland who gained Pomerelia in 1294 and was crowned King of Poland at Gniezno in 1295, the first royal coronation in Poland for over two centuries. He was murdered at Rogoźno in February 1296, probably by agents of Brandenburg, and his lands…

pshemakho-kotsev.s: Pshemakho Kotsev was a Kabardian politician who led the government of the Mountainous Republic of the Northern Caucasus in 1918–1919. He sought a federal democratic state of the mountain peoples, independent of Russia, but the republic was crushed between the Bolsheviks and…

purdil-khan.s: Purdil Khan was the eldest of the Kandahar Sardars, Barakzai brothers who took Kandahar after the Durrani Empire broke up in 1818. A half-brother of Dost Mohammad Khan of Kabul, he led the brothers' joint rule of the principality until his death in 1830, when Kohandil Khan…

pushpa-kamal-dahal.s: Pushpa Kamal Dahal, known as Prachanda, led the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) through its insurgency against the monarchy from 1996 to 2006. After the peace agreement the Maoists won the 2008 elections that abolished the monarchy, and he became the republic's first prime…

pyotr-masherov.s: Pyotr Masherov was a Soviet Belarusian leader, a partisan commander in the Second World War and Hero of the Soviet Union. As first secretary of the Communist Party of Byelorussia from 1965 to 1980 he oversaw rapid industrial growth and the commemoration of the war.

pyramid-texts.s: The Pyramid Texts are the oldest Egyptian religious writings, spells carved on the walls of the burial chambers of pyramids to help the king reach the afterlife. They first appear in the pyramid of Unas, last king of the Fifth Dynasty, and were used by later Old Kingdom kings…

pyrrhus-of-epirus.s: Pyrrhus was a king of the Molossians and of Epirus, sheltered as an infant by the Taulantian king Glaukias. Invited by Taras in 280 BCE, he defeated Rome at Heraclea and Asculum at such cost that a 'Pyrrhic victory' became proverbial.

pythian-games.s: The Pythian Games were the festival of Apollo at Delphi, one of the four Panhellenic games of ancient Greece. Reorganised by the Amphictyonic League in 582 BCE after the First Sacred War, they were held every four years and, unlike the Olympics, included contests in music and…
